prize_parts.citation: For theoretical prediction and experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall effect and the topological insulator state of matter

statement.case_for: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators identified a genuinely new class of electronic matter, defined by a Z2 topological invariant and protected edge and surface states. The history is the theory-then-experiment sequence a materials physicist most trusts: Kane and Mele's Z2 classification and graphene proposal, then Molenkamp's group observing quantised edge transport in HgTe quantum wells, followed by many independent confirmations in transport and ARPES in several material families. Two decades of reproduction and a stable interpretation make this the most mature of the condensed-matter candidates, and it is the one where the discovery, rather than a technology built on it, is the centre of the citation. Topology has since spread into photonics, cold atoms and magnetism, which supports lasting impact.
statement.case_against: The credit is not clean. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang made the HgTe prediction that Molenkamp's experiment tested, and the three-dimensional topological insulator work of Fu, Kane, Moore, Balents and Hasan is outside the trio. Several colleagues have called this a real attribution problem, and I agree it is the main weakness. There is also overlap with the 2016 prize for topological phases, and the quantised-edge evidence in HgTe is more delicate than the topology concept. If the committee judges that a three-name cap cannot honour the field fairly, B008 is the cleanest fallback because its credit is unambiguous.

responses.point: Ranked B049 third but called the omission of Zhang, Bernevig, Hughes, Moore, Fu and Hasan a real attribution problem, making the trio defensible but contested; deferred to condensed-matter colleagues.
responses.response: I accept the omission is real and I do not want to wave it away. My reading is that the discovery in the citation is the quantum spin Hall effect: Kane and Mele supplied the topological theory, and Molenkamp supplied the experiment. BHZ made a predictive step that guided the experiment, but the Z2 concept and the QSH state came from Kane and Mele first. A prize on this core follows the prior of crediting the original idea plus the decisive demonstration. I would keep 3D topological insulators as a separate possible achievement for later. Zhang's death also removes him from eligibility, which makes the cleanest trio a bit more defensible than it first looks. I would still like your view, as someone close to the experimental side, on whether Molenkamp's HgTe result stands as decisive without BHZ.

responses.point: Ranked B049 second, called it mature and arguably overdue, but noted the disputed priority between Kane-Mele and parallel 2005-2006 work, and the missing HgTe proposers.
responses.response: I largely agree on maturity, and I appreciate that you rank it high while naming the priority issue. On priority, Kane and Mele's two 2005 papers predate the BHZ proposal and the Fu-Kane-Mele and Moore-Balents work, so their claim to the Z2 classification and the QSH idea is, on my reading, the earliest. I have not independently verified the parallel 2005-2006 claims, and a committee investigation of the papers would be needed. I differ from your first place, B011: KPZ universality is elegant and the Takeuchi experiment is clean, but the confirmation rests largely on one liquid-crystal setup and the theory credit omits Parisi. Because of that, I think it is less secure as a prize than the topological case.

responses.point: Ranked B008 first as a clean atomic-physics invention where she can judge the systematic-shift calculations, but ranked B049 sixth because of the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang.
responses.response: Your reading of the optical lattice clock is persuasive. I rank it as my main alternative, since the 10^-18 performance has been confirmed by several independent groups and the two names are close to uncontroversial. Where I differ is the weight of the attribution problem. B008 does leave Lemonde, Ludlow, Sterr and the ion-clock lineage, so it is not free of credit questions either. And I weigh a new state of matter above an inventive measurement tool, given the earlier prizes for combs in 2005 and ion clocks in 2012. That said, I would not object to B008 as the committee's outcome, and I would value a view from you on whether the SI second redefinition is better waited for.

responses.point: Ranked B008 first, stressing relativistic geodesy, constants tests and dark-matter searches, with the credit line drawn around the invention and its leading realisation.
responses.response: I find that framing fair, and the clean allocation is a real advantage over B049. My reservation is whether the tests of constants and geodesy have actually yielded a discovery so far, or a promise of one. With a clock prize the concern is that most of the physics payoff is still prospective. For topological insulators the physics is already in hand and confirmed by spectroscopy. I would also like to know how you view the 2005 and 2012 prizes as overlap, since several colleagues raised it.

uncertainties: Whether Kane and Mele's priority for the Z2 classification and QSH proposal over the parallel 2005-2006 work holds up under closer reading of the papers; my recollection is not independently verified here.
Whether the committee prefers a prize confined to the 2D quantum spin Hall effect or one that must also cover 3D topological insulators, which would break the three-person cap.
Overlap with the 2016 prize for topological phases and phase transitions.
Whether an optical lattice clock is judged by its realised physics discoveries or by its measurement capability, which affects how I weigh B008 as an alternative.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I have no known personal or institutional tie to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp or the other shortlisted candidates. My Uppsala theoretical magnetism work is in adjacent condensed-matter areas, which I note only as proximity.
